body: Bangladeshi licence plates are either white, black or turquoise. The turquoise plate is unique to Bangladesh.
The Bengali script features a continuous horizontal line at the top of each word and many letters with triangular shapes. It is an official language in Bangladesh and parts of eastern India.
In Generation 3 coverage, look for three cars: the red mirror with bars, classic white, and striped white car. Only the classic white car is not unique to Bangladesh.
In Generation 4 coverage, two Street View cars can be seen: a black car and a white car.
Bangladesh has some poor quality "Shitcam" coverage from black and white cars, sometimes with a big circular blur.
Rickshaws, especially green auto rickshaws, are frequently found all around Bangladesh.
Signposts in Bangladesh often have black-and-white stripes, similar to several other Asian countries.
Bodies of water and agricultural fields are often seen beside the streets of Bangladesh.
Streets in Bangladesh are often lined by trees, which sometimes have white paint on the bottom of their trunks.
Bangladesh uses circular or square red-and-white concrete bollards.
Tin roofs are commonly found in Bangladesh and other humid South and Southeast Asian countries.
The Generation 4 coverage in Bangladesh often has a smoky feel to it.
Western Bangladesh, including Rajshahi, Khulna and Dhaka, is dominated by hip roofs made of sheet metal, while the east has more varied styles.
In eastern Bangladesh, especially Sylhet, you will commonly see sheet metal roofs with a triangular "window" just below the ridge.
Tiled roofs are uncommon, but can be found on the Indian border in the state of Khulna.
Early growth rice, which is short and green, can be seen in Khulna, Mymensingh, and south of the Padma River in Dhaka.
Slightly taller, mid-growth green rice can be seen in Rangpur, Barishal, and Chittagong.
Fully-grown rice is taller with a yellow or orange color and is mostly seen in Rajshahi, but also in Rangpur and Chittagong.
Harvested rice is short and beige or brown, most commonly seen in Sylhet and southern Khulna.
Off-season barren rice fields are mostly seen in the state of Dhaka, north of the Padma River.
Vast, empty rice fields can be seen in the border area between Dhaka, Mymensingh, and Sylhet.
While most of Bangladesh is flat, the eastern parts of Chittagong have tall, forested hills.
A sizable east-west ridge can be seen on the Indian border from northern Sylhet and eastern Mymensingh.
Corn is mainly planted in western Bangladesh, particularly in Rajshahi, Rangpur, western Mymensingh, and northern Khulna.
Jute, a tall green crop, is almost exclusively found on Street View in Rangpur.
Canola, a low-growing crop with yellow flowers, is extremely common north of the Padma river in the state of Dhaka.
Tea production is concentrated in the highlands of southern Sylhet and, rarely, Chittagong.
Standalone fruit trees and fruit orchards are most commonly seen in Rajshahi and Rangpur, especially near the Indian border.
Sunflower fields are found in the south of Barishal state.
Fields of watermelons can also be found in the south of Barishal.
Eucalyptus trees, with their tall, ivory-coloured trunks, are more common in the northern states of Rangpur, Rajshahi, and Mymensingh.
Blossoming trees in Generation 4 coverage are found in Khulna, Mymensingh, and southern Dhaka, where coverage was taken during springtime.
Beach Sheoaks are thin evergreen trees observed in coastal regions, like the Teknaf Peninsula and around Noakhali city in Chittagong.
Generation 4 coverage with a 2022 copyright label can be found in Mymensingh, Dhaka, and less commonly Chittagong.
Generation 4 coverage with a 2023 copyright label can be found in Rangpur, Rajshahi, Khulna, Barishal, Sylhet, and less commonly Chittagong.
Shitcam coverage is only found in and around Dhaka.
Generation 3 coverage with the white Street View car can be found in Dhaka, Chattogram, and on the highway connecting them.
Generation 3 coverage with the striped Street View car can be found mostly on yellow roads west of Dhaka.
In Sylhet city's Generation 3 coverage, a guard holding a hayfork is often visible at the side of the car.
In Barishal city, a guard can also be visible at the side of the car.
A trekker with a black cover can be found in the city of Khulna.
The trekker with red colour in the mirrors is unique to the island of Nijhum Dwip.
A scooter trekker with a visible left mirror and some hair can be found on Hatiya Island.
A trekker escorted by a security guard is found on Saint Martin's Island.
